safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce from SAP 3.0 days — explicit safety stock makes the ERP lead-time buffer redundant

narrative: Material PL1__MD2C777C shows consistently high erratic demand (~1,942 units/day, CV=0.209) with no significant trend over the 216-day observation window. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.575, range 0.04–6.03 days), making lead-time variance the dominant driver of buffer requirements. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with a 6,573-unit EOQ-derived order quantity and a 4,217-unit safety stock sized at the 95th percentile of demand-during-lead-time delivers full service-level compliance within storage capacity while reducing total inventory costs by 96.4% versus the current MOQ-only SAP baseline.
warnings: Lead time CV=0.575 classified as UNSTABLE — safety stock is intentionally elevated to compensate; supplier engagement recommended to reduce lead time variability.

research_insights.selection_rationale: High-volume, near-continuous daily demand (non-zero fraction=100%, mean ~1,942 units/day) makes a continuous-review trigger policy appropriate. EOQ minimises total ordering+holding cost; the reorder point absorbs lead-time and demand uncertainty at the target service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding (max post-replenishment inventory 10,790 vs. limit 12,057). No capacity-driven service degradation expected.
